dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, are you here to compete in The Crux Clash?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: You bet I am, have you put your names down yet?

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Well, I'd have a look at the entrance criteria if I were you. They don't allow just anyone to take part.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: The Clash is a comprehensive test of fighting ability. Anyone who turns up for show over skill is gonna get their butt handed to them.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Tsk, nobody wants to see that, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we heard a rule about that. So Paimon's wondering... are you a renowned fighter?

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Hahaha, me? Only a former runner-up in the Chihu Rock Freestyle Combat Summit! Oh yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... Also, that doesn't sound like the most official tournament out there...

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: What!? You... Nonsense! Have you been living under a rock? It's been going on for years! There were plenty of competitors when I took part!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Not to mention, I've helped the Millelith catch Treasure Hoarders before! There were two of them trying to escape — I soon sorted them out.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: They tried to sneak past me under the cover of darkness... Ha! They didn't know what hit 'em.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I planted a left hook on the skinnier one's face and sent him flying. Then, the big guy pulled out a knife!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I stood my ground, of course. A roundhouse kick sent the blade hurtling into a beam above us.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: Hahaha, I told you! Unarmed, outnumbered two to one, but I still got the upper hand!

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I'm not saying I came out completely unscathed of course, but the fact remains that I did manage to subdue the both of them... AND hand them over to the Millelith. I received quite the commendation! Oh yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh... But for us, even four or five Treasure Hoarders at a time is all in a day's work...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thanks for letting us know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm... Alright, we're gonna keep looking around.

response.speaker: Uncle Yun
response.text: I'll see you in the arena. Tsk, but I don't plan on losing to a pair of children any time soon!

choices.text: We just wanted to take a look around first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, are you here for The Crux Clash too?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: That's right. Nothing beats real-life combat for honing your skills. That's what our master taught us.

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: But this tournament is more than just a chance to put training into practice — it's also a chance for us to obtain the Masterless Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Exactly! With a Vision, we'd quickly become our master's top students.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This master of yours must be pretty incredible, huh... Are they someone famous?

dialogues.speaker: Chai Yi
dialogues.text: Famous? He's the founder of the Lingshan Clan, and his skills are unparalleled! Liang and I are both proud disciples of his.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: You probably wouldn't have heard of it, it was founded quite recently. The clan is nowhere near as famous as the master himself, anyway.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: He's got to be a grandmaster or something. He's created many different styles of kung fu, and countless other clans have borrowed extensively from him.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: To the Lingshan Clan, he teaches a special technique known as "force dispersal."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Force dispersal"?

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It's a type of breathing exercise where you can train yourself to harness the energy around you and neutralize attacks without moving an inch.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: For example, our master can use it to alter the path of an attacking fist, or change the direction of an incoming stone, all without breaking a sweat!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: One time, he sent a challenger flying into the air without lifting a finger!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that really possible?

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: It sure is! But it's extremely difficult to cultivate this ability. We've been training for ages, and we're still getting to grips with the very basics. There's no way we could use it proficiently yet.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: *sigh* We're clearly not that naturally gifted, or we would have at least gotten the gist by now... If we don't start making progress soon, we'll probably run out of money to pay the tuition fees and still have nothing to show for all our training...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a tuition fee!?

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Of course! This is a grandmaster we're talking about here. He doesn't have time to waste. If you want face-to-face training, you've gotta show you're sincere about it.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: *sigh* But here we are, having trained under him directly all this time without even a hint of improvement. Master is getting increasingly impatient with us.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Recently, though, we heard that a Vision bearer joined the Guhua Clan and made pretty much instant progress in their training.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: So, if we can get our hands on a Vision, too, maybe we can finally make our master proud!

choices.text: A Vision won't make you better at martial arts.

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: Well, we have to try something new, otherwise, we're stuck in the same situation.

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Exactly, it can't hurt to try. And if it turns out it does work, the Lingshan Clan will go down in history!

response.speaker: Liang
response.text: Folks will come from far and wide. Heck, we could even become the dominant martial arts clan in all of Liyue!

response.speaker: Chai Yi
response.text: See you in the arena!

choices.text: There may be other reasons why you can't seem to master this technique...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Qingce Village Armwrestling Champion, huh... *sigh* Alright, you're signed up...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Next please... what's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... Wait! A—Aren't you...!?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #Did I hear that right? {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: Is it really them?

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Aren't they a Vision bearer, though? Why are they trying to enter The Clash?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Uh... I—I have to ask... aren't you the traveler that helped Liyue fight off that ancient god...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #It's really {F#her}{M#him}!

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: The one that spoke with Lady Keqing at the Rite of Parting!

dialogues.speaker: Clash Competitor
dialogues.text: #Oh! Oh! I wonder if I can get {F#her}{M#his} autograph later?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: I—I trust you are aware that... only those without Visions can enter the tournament?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't have a Vision.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Really? B—But from what I've heard, the things you're capable of in combat are... nothing short of extraordinary... You walk into the most dangerous situations imaginable, face off against all sorts of monsters — even the Fatui — and always come out on top!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yup! {F#She}{M#He} still doesn't have a Vision though. See for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: My apologies, I didn't mean to be rude. I'm sure a great hero like yourself would have no reason to lie. Now, could I ask you to provide a few claims to fame?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: It's just a formality for you, of course, but I have to make a record of competitors' achievements as part of the sign-up process...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: So far I've got "Defeated the ancient god, Osial," so that's one. Do you... have any others?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and also a dragon, too! Put down "Battle with Stormterror"!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: #Might as well declare {F#her}{M#him} the champion already.

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: I wonder if it's too late to withdraw?

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Okay, um... that's plenty... Actually, this is the most dazzling track record I've ever seen, by a long shot...

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Right, your registration is complete. Now, a brief word about the prize.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: A great hero such as yourself can surely only be here for one thing — to win the tournament and claim the grand prize, namely, a Vision.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we're not here for that. We're here because Captain Beidou promised to take us to Inazuma if we win the tournament.

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: There's another prize too? First I've heard of it!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: Beidou must have upped the stakes this time to attract top talent!

response.speaker: Clash Competitor
response.text: But why would anyone want to go somewhere as dangerous as Inazuma?

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: ...I see, so... I take it you discussed your terms with Beidou in advance, then.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Well, nobody expected you to sign up to a tournament like this... I can hardly believe it myself, to be honest...

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Anyway, the qualifying rounds are about to begin. I'll leave you to your preparation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, so, Paimon's thinking about that whole "no Vision bearers" rule in this tournament.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though you don't have a Vision, most people in Teyvat think that you can't manipulate the elements without one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Paimon thinks you probably shouldn't use your elemental abilities during the tournament. Y'know, just to avoid any misunderstandings.

choices.text: I'm just not that interested in Visions, that's all.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Well, I'm sure a great hero has an important reason for being here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, put that down! And also, "Defeated the Fatui Harbinger, Childe."

choices.text: I'm the Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Also, don't forget to mention that previous battles include, but are not limited to "Stormterror" Dvalin and Fatui Harbinger, Childe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In any case, looking at the competition, it should still be pretty easy for you to win even without using any elements, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, it's showtime! You got this!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: You seem like you're raring to go. Are you ready to compete?

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Good, then please follow me into the arena.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Not a problem, there's still time. Make sure you're fully prepared!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: Your opponent in the semi-finals is new to The Crux Clash, but he has quickly become the dark horse of the tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuhan
dialogues.text: I do not doubt your abilities, but I would suggest that you make sure you are fully prepared before you begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Relax! My {F#girl}{M#guy}'s at the top of {F#her}{M#his} game, {F#she}{M#he} ain't gonna lose!

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Okay. Follow me.

choices.text: Interesting... getting a few butterflies over here.

response.speaker: Zhuhan
response.text: Don't worry, take some time to compose yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you, haha! I watched your match. What a stunning performance!

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: I myself was eliminated in the third round. *sigh* Shame... If only I could have advanced one more round...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, maybe next time, huh? By the way, do you happen to know who else advanced to the final round?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: Why, yes. He's the same one who defeated me. He is a formidable opponent, quick on his feet and swift to take advantage of his opponent's missteps.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: I faltered for but a brief moment, but before I knew it, he had me on the floor.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: Given my stature, I have no fear of squaring off with physically strong opponents. But faced with a nimble, agile opponent such as him... I found myself completely out of my league...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Yun
dialogues.text: Still — I'm sure he'll be no match for you, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there... uh, but where did the other guy go?

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: He tried to use force dispersal to deflect a punch, but instead he took it straight to the nose. There was blood all over the place...

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: His opponent was pretty freaked out by it. He kept asking him "why didn't you dodge?" But he was pretty much out cold by that point and couldn't reply.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: "Why don't you dodge?" they ask... Because to not dodge is the very essence of Lingshan Clan kung fu. It's just that he hadn't quite mastered it yet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did your match go?

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Don't even get me started... I spent all my energy helping him get from here to the boat to take him back to the harbor. But by the time I got back, my scheduled match time had already passed, and I had to forfeit.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: I don't dare tell my master about this... Otherwise, I'd never hear the end of it.

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Sorry, I shouldn't be complaining in front of you like this. I'm afraid I'm still a bit out of sorts at the moment, so I probably won't be able to help you with whatever you were here to ask me about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, alright then... hope your buddy makes a swift recovery. Hang in there!

dialogues.speaker: Liang
dialogues.text: Thanks, I'll do my best...

dialogues.speaker: Clitopho
dialogues.text: Thanks for saving me! I was beginning to think that I might become dog food at this rate...

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Hey now, that's not a good joke.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And how did you end up in this sorry state?

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Me? I was helping Erge out... But I screwed up and got chucked into this cage.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Him? He's from Mingyun Village. Used to work over there. After they ran the ore veins dry, he came to The Chasm. Did pretty well too. Made foreman, I believe.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Then... you know the story. The Chasm went "woosh," and the miners went "whoa," and the Ministry of Civil Affairs did a "Hmm? Hmm? Hmm?"

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: And the Qixing bigwigs did a "ahem-ahem!" and the Millelith came and went "hmph-hmph-hmph!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the heck is this guy saying?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Try speaking the common tongue, please.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Well, in the end, the mine was closed and the miners went out of work. And when miners get put out of a job, what do you think they'll do they do to make ends meet, hmm?

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Well, what I'm saying is Erge was an experienced miner who barely ever saw the light of day in his life, and who had just made foreman at 40... and then suddenly, it was all gone!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: So, what would he do, and where?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, join... the Treasure Hoarders?

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Exactly! See, now you're thinking like a Hoarder!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: But lemme give you some sage advice: it might be best not to do anything illegal. The Treasure Hoarders aren't good people, no, not at all. And there's no going back once you've gone too far into a life of crime...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh, that's right... Paimon won't ever become a Treasure Hoarder...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: —Which is pretty rich, coming from you!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Hahahaha! I mean... Well, let's not joke about this anymore. In any case, what I meant to say was that people don't necessarily join the Treasure Hoarders because of some inherent evil in their hearts.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: But for Erge, the compensation from the Ministry of Civil Affairs should have been enough to let him start over in an honest profession, and yet he chose this path.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: I guess to each his own, huh? Maybe some people just can't take the pain in the short term, and choose a perilous road of bringing others pain instead. Perhaps this is what we'd call "the other side of freedom" back in Mondstadt.

choices.text: So, tell me about, well, you.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Me? Just me? I'm no one important.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: I'm from Mondstadt, and I haven't been a Hoarder long, nor have I been in Liyue long. I just came with a few senior members to get some ore.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: I was following Erge around, doing some errands, helping them sneak around a bit, contacting our comrades down in the mines... and then, you know, I got caught by you while doing those things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not correct. You were in this cage well before we caught you doing anything.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: *sigh* Well, I mucked up on one of my tasks, which caused our lads to get ambushed by someone...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Now that was us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehe...

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: So that was really... I knew it was you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it was nothing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And anyway, we didn't know how you'd get involved in the whole thing, either.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Ugh... Anyway, I was sent by Erge to keep watch on our Weasel Thieves after that... And I made another mistake in allowing them to run amok. They stole all our stuff...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pfft... Hahaha!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Yes, yes, keep laughing. Just make sure your stomach stays in one piece while you're at it... Ugh, that was embarrassing.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Still after that, Erge sent me down to find some secret passage. I did find it... and then the earthquake happened! Nearly buried us all alive, too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You know what? I think... that might have been us, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right! That must've happened when we destroyed... uh, unsealed the Bedrock Keys. It was a pretty big earthquake, too!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: And if Erge was mad at me before, now he was absolutely hopping mad!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: "You worthless piece of trash! I'll bet the Millelith sent you here to sabotage us, didn't they?"

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: "And you did wreck us, didn't you? Let our Weasel Thieves run off, did you? Boys, put him in the Weasel Thief cage! We'll settle scores with him once we're done with this transaction!"

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: ...That's what he said.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: And then he locked me in this cage. Might have forgotten to mention that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahahahaha! Paimon almost feels bad for Erge!

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Well, yes, he did get slapped around by the two of you. Twice.

response.speaker: Clitopho
response.text: Not... not that I'm feeling sorry for him, of course! I'm just glad that you came to my rescue. I'd be dead meat otherwise.

choices.text: Ah, what a shame that we don't keep dogs either.

dialogues.speaker: Khedive
dialogues.text: #Hello, {NICKNAME}! It's great to see you here.

response.speaker: Khedive
response.text: A field study, to record and research ancient life forms and their remains. Well, and I'm also here to observe the abnormalities in the geological layers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And you're not going down there yourself?

response.speaker: Khedive
response.text: Me? Go down there? No, of course not.

response.speaker: Khedive
response.text: I mean, I did pay for this exploration team to be set up. I'll fork out the Mora, you do the work. My research gets done, you get paid. I'm happy, you're happy. See?

response.speaker: Khedive
response.text: That's how that works.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...This guy is really annoying.

response.speaker: Khedive
response.text: Well, don't let me keep you too long.

dialogues.speaker: Taliesin
dialogues.text: #We meet again, golden-haired {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Taliesin, have you come for a duel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what are you saying?

response.speaker: Taliesin
response.text: Haha, I'm here to get some inspiration, of course! Listen to this: the hero without a past, bereft of any clan, and their loyal fairy retainer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No idea who you're talking about.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yup. No idea here either.

response.speaker: Taliesin
response.text: Look, look! O modest hero, do not cast your perplexed gaze towards the distant mountains, for in this benighted land, you are the very light itself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What...?

response.speaker: Taliesin
response.text: I'm talking about you! In my current written template, of course.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so this guy can actually say things we understand.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you.

response.speaker: Taliesin
response.text: #See you, gold-haired {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's follow that adeptus's instructions and search for the scattered adeptal energy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Ooh, look! The pearl over there has lit up, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Ooh, look! The pearl over there has lit up, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you wait in silence for some time, young shoots slowly emerge from the soil...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, do you wanna try your hand at Pankration? Why don't we ask someone how to enter the tournament?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's head to the Pankration Ring and take it from there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It looks like there's a path here. Paimon wonders where it'll lead to...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... it doesn't look like we have any other clues, so wanna just try and see where it leads?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will there be one up there? But how should we get up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon doesn't like this place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just what is this place exactly? It's like a maze...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some Flying Squirrels came over... Looks like they love Quenepa Berries, huh?
